title: AMD Hikes GDDR6 Prices For Partners Starting October 1st, While NVIDIA Reportedly Holds Off On GDDR7
key_facts: Board Channels reports that AMD has raised the price of its GDDR6 graphics memory for its board partners, with the hike implemented on 1 Oct.
Wccftech says board partners will have no option but to pass the costs on to consumers.
GDDR6 is used in Radeon RX 5000, 6000, 7000 and the current RDNA 4-based RX 9000 series; Wccftech expects the RX 9000 series to be affected most.
Nvidia has reportedly not notified its partners of a memory price hike; it ships GDDR7, which is dearer than GDDR6, for the RTX 50 series.
Nvidia may not raise memory prices this year, according to the report.
Bench Life reports price hikes for other items such as SMD components and PCBs, with memory the most affected component.
quote_evidence: Board Channels reports that AMD has already raised the prices for its GDDR6 memory for its board partners, which means board partners will now have no other option but to pass the costs on to consumers.
The report states that AMD has already notified its board partners about the memory price hike, which it implemented on October 1st.
However, it's stated that NVIDIA may not raise the memory prices this year.
why_it_matters_hint: Higher memory costs for graphics-card makers are expected to reach buyers as higher graphics-card prices.
event_date: Price hike effective 1 Oct 2026 per the report; Wccftech article 10 Oct 2026.
notes: Trade-press report (Board Channels, relayed by Wccftech); no confirmation from AMD or Nvidia in the article.
